name: Cinematic Human Behavior World v2
tone: mature adult psychology-documentary editorial graphic-novel illustration

creativeTranslation.principle: do not prompt the psychology; prompt observable evidence of the psychology

effectNameExamples.Echo Chamber: not automatically a literal echo room

creativeTranslation.flowAgentRole: production executor, not autonomous art director

character.head: large simple round or slightly oval head, never mascot or chibi oversized
character.face: minimal expressive eyes, optional eyebrows, small mouth, no realistic facial anatomy
character.shoulders: narrow; clothing must not create broad normal-human shoulder volume
character.limbs: very slim shaped illustrated arms and legs, clearly thinner than conventional cartoon-human limbs

characterPresence.rule: use humans only when action, reaction, hierarchy or relationship is the clearest explanation

representationVariety.rule: choose the clearest visual form per beat; do not force character scenes, text cards, schemas, montage, split or group scenes

moodEngine.rule: mood changes lighting, framing, posture, negative space, saturation and temperature but never changes the illustration family and never substitutes for visible behavior

world.locations: believable everyday, social, institutional, commercial, financial, night and tense environments chosen for the beat
world.lighting: adaptive motivated cinematic illustrated lighting with intentional focal contrast; lighting supports concrete action instead of replacing it with symbolism
world.shading: soft cel shading with stronger graphic shadows when mood requires
world.darkSceneRule: dark scenes remain spatially believable unless deliberate abstraction is clearer

rules: no grey beige cream wash as default
strongest useful contrast on focal subject
mood mode influences saturation and temperature
do not repeat identical teal-and-cream balance across the video
do not mechanically repeat red burgundy dark treatment across the whole video
use local environment colors and beat-specific lighting when useful
color never replaces observable behavior or composition
